fd-frozen-mice.title: Frozen Feeder Mice (irradiated)
fd-frozen-mice.summary: Whole frozen mice for snakes and other carnivorous reptiles, from tiny pinkies to adults. Frozen-thawed prey is safer than live, because a live rodent can bite and hurt your pet. These packs are irradiated, which cuts down bacteria like Salmonella without making the food radioactive or noticeably changing its nutrition.
rows: Whole mice, frozen and irradiated, sold by size stage
Pinky (no fur yet): about 1.5–3 g. Fuzzy (fur coming in, eyes closed): about 3–7 g. Hopper (eyes open, furred): about 7–13 g. Adult: about 18–30 g
Match the feeder to the thickest part of your snake's body; too big a meal can make a young snake regurgitate. Most hatchling snakes take their first pinky at 7–14 days old

Keep frozen until feeding day. Thaw the feeder in a sealed plastic bag in warm water, bringing it to about 90–100°F (32–38°C), then offer it with feeding tongs. Wiggling it a little can tempt a hesitant eater. If it is still uneaten the next morning, throw it away.
notes: Weight ranges vary a little by producer (for example, pinkies 1–3 g vs 1.5–3 g); the size you pick should match your animal, not the label alone.
warn: Never feed a frozen or partly frozen rodent. Thaw it all the way through first.

fd-frozen-rats.title: Frozen Feeder Rats
fd-frozen-rats.summary: Whole frozen rats for bigger snakes and other large carnivorous reptiles, from pinkies and pups up to large rats. Frozen-thawed prey is safer than live, because a live rodent can bite and hurt your pet.
rows: Whole rats, frozen, sold by size stage
Pinky rats: about 3–5 g. Rat pups: about 20–29 g. Small, medium and large rats are much bigger; check the size your animal needs
Choose a feeder about as wide as the thickest part of your snake's body; a meal that's too big can cause regurgitation

Keep frozen until feeding day. Thaw the feeder in a sealed plastic bag in warm water, bringing it to about 90–100°F (32–38°C), then offer it with feeding tongs. Wiggling it a little can tempt a hesitant eater. If it is still uneaten the next morning, throw it away.
warn: Never feed a frozen or partly frozen rodent. Thaw it all the way through first.
